definitions.plain_definition: Refers to Emmy Noether, a mathematician who proved that every conservation law (like conservation of energy) comes from a symmetry in nature.
definitions.used_in_context: Noether did not end the question. She sharpened it.

definitions.plain_definition: A rule in physics that says some quantity (like energy or charge) stays the same over time, even as things change.
definitions.used_in_context: Conservation laws feel final because they never seem to break.

definitions.plain_definition: A property of a system that stays the same when you change something about it, like rotating a perfect circle.
definitions.used_in_context: If conservation law stands on symmetry, then symmetry is the new floor.

definitions.plain_definition: Provides a foundation or reason for something to exist or be true.
definitions.used_in_context: The deeper question is what grounds the symmetry that grounds them.

definitions.plain_definition: A clear, logical reason or mathematical origin for a rule.
definitions.used_in_context: The law is not free-floating. It has a formal source.

definitions.plain_definition: The quality of being able to be measured or quantified.
definitions.used_in_context: The deepest layer is the source of measurability

definitions.plain_definition: A made-up term in this document that combines theology and physics to ask about the ultimate foundation of physical laws.
definitions.used_in_context: Physics reaches symmetry. Theophysics asks what grounds the symmetry.

definitions.plain_definition: A step-by-step logical or mathematical process to reach a conclusion.
definitions.used_in_context: Read the full derivation in The Floor Beneath the Floor
